abstract: Robust routing under uncertainty is central to real-world logistics, yet most benchmarks assume static, idealized settings. We present \texttt{SVRPBench}, the first open benchmark to capture high-fidelity stochastic dynamics in vehicle routing at urban scale. Spanning more than 500 instances with up to 1000 customers, it simulates realistic delivery conditions: time-dependent congestion, log-normal delays, probabilistic accidents, and empirically grounded time windows for residential and commercial clients. Our pipeline generates diverse, constraint-rich scenarios, including multi-depot and multi-vehicle setups. Benchmarking reveals that state-of-the-art RL solvers like POMO and AM degrade by over 20\% under distributional shift, while classical and metaheuristic methods remain robust. To enable reproducible research, we release the dataset ( Huggingface ) and evaluation suite ( Github ). SVRPBench challenges the community to design solvers that generalize beyond synthetic assumptions and adapt to real-world uncertainty.
title: SVRPBench: A Realistic Benchmark for Stochastic Vehicle Routing Problem

abstract: We study which machine learning algorithms have tight generalization bounds with respect to a given collection of population distributions. Our results build on and extend the recent work of Gastpar et al. (2023). First, we present conditions that preclude the existence of tight generalization bounds. Specifically, we show that algorithms that have certain inductive biases that cause them to be unstable do not admit tight generalization bounds. Next, we show that algorithms that are sufficiently loss-stable do have tight generalization bounds. We conclude with a simple characterization that relates the existence of tight generalization bounds to the conditional variance of the algorithm's loss.

summary.idea: The paper studies how stability connects to the existence of such bounds. It analyzes both destabilizing inductive biases and sufficient stability of the algorithm's loss.
summary.limitations: The conclusions are relative to a specified distribution collection and technical notions of stability. The abstract does not provide a practical procedure for obtaining tight bounds for an arbitrary deployed model.
summary.problem: A generalization bound is useful only if it closely reflects how an algorithm performs on unseen data. Some algorithms may not admit tight bounds over a chosen family of distributions.
summary.results: Certain forms of instability rule out tight generalization bounds, while sufficient loss stability permits them. A final characterization relates this possibility to the conditional variance of the algorithm's loss.
summary.tldr: Whether tight generalization guarantees exist depends on an algorithm's stability and the variability of its loss.

title: Which Algorithms Have Tight Generalization Bounds?
